overview: Oil did the heavy lifting on Friday. Brent rose about 3.6% to near $110 as Iran stepped up attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, capping a week in which WTI gained more than 10%. Coal followed energy higher, trading near a three-year high as costly LNG pushes Asian and European buyers back to coal before winter.

Metals were mixed. A 2% drop on the Nasdaq sent money into bonds, and lower yields steadied gold near $4,166, though it still closed the week down. Silver and palladium slipped, platinum rose, and copper ended a three-day losing streak on Chilean mine disruptions. Grains kept sliding under harvest pressure, with corn at an eight-week low and soybeans at a seven-week low. Bitcoin held near $82,000 after Thursday's liquidations.

watchItems.title: Hormuz flow revisions
watchItems.text: Kpler counts 11.6M b/d; CENTCOM's figure implies about 14.3M. Revised data will show which is closer. Affects the Oil and Hormuz pages.

watchItems.title: EIA inventories, Wednesday
watchItems.text: The first report since US strategic reserve releases ended. Another large crude draw would support oil.

watchItems.title: Fed, Oct 27–28
watchItems.text: October hike odds are low, December is near 90%. Rate expectations are driving gold, silver, platinum and palladium more than inflation itself.

watchItems.title: US harvest pace
watchItems.text: Corn was 33% harvested and soybeans 46% as of Oct 11. A fast finish adds pressure to the Corn, Wheat and Soybean pages.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold held near $4,166 on Friday. A 2% Nasdaq drop pushed money into bonds and lower yields steadied the metal, but it still closed the week lower after Wednesday's hot CPI briefly sent it below $4,100. Markets price about a 92% chance of a December Fed hike, which is capping rallies. It sits about 26% below January's record of $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver slipped 0.7% to just under $57, extending a 12.6% monthly decline. Safe-haven buying during Friday's equity selloff was not enough to offset rate-hike expectations. The metal is now more than half below its late-January record near $121.6, even as the Silver Institute projects a sixth straight supply deficit this year.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent jumped about 3.6% to near $110 and WTI gained 4% to $101.84, capping a week in which WTI rose more than 10%. At least nine ships were attacked near Hormuz, Houthi missiles targeted Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian refineries. US crude stocks fell 8.6 million barrels and emergency reserve releases have ended.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper rose 0.3% to $6.53 a pound, ending a three-session losing streak. A weaker dollar helped, and Chilean supply tightened with strikes at BHP's Escondida and Antofagasta's Centinela plus weather disruption at Codelco's El Teniente. Demand from data centres and grid storage keeps it close to September's record of $6.85.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal edged up 0.5% to $150.40 a tonne, near a three-year high and up about 45% on the year. Middle East disruption has made LNG expensive, and with coal about 80% cheaper, Asian and European utilities are stocking up before winter. Indonesia, the largest exporter, has tightened export rules and its August shipments fell 23%.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum rose 0.7% to $1,633 but remains near a three-month low after a 9% monthly drop. Safe-haven demand helped on Friday while higher-for-longer rate expectations weighed. A 2% fall in global EV sales in September could support autocatalyst demand, but the WPIC still expects total platinum demand to fall 18% this year.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium fell 0.9% to $1,118.50, its lowest in over a year, and is down 14% on the month and 25% on the year. Steady investment outflows and rate-hike expectations are weighing, and EVs continue to erode catalytic-converter demand. South African power problems and Russia trade risks limit supply, but not enough to offset falling demand.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: Iran escalated attacks this week, with at least nine ships hit near the strait since Sunday and the container ship GFS Pride sunk on Wednesday. Kpler measured 11.6 million barrels a day in the week to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war level; CENTCOM's figure implies about 14.3 million. Supertanker rates are around $1.3 million a day.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: Corn fell 0.8% to 474¢, near an eight-week low. The USDA raised its US yield estimate to 181.2 bushels an acre and projects ending stocks of 1.85 billion bushels, outweighing a slow harvest (33% done vs the five-year average 39%) and a 25-million-bushel increase in the export forecast.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: CBOT wheat dropped about 1.5% to 660¢, near a two-month low, though still up about 31% on the year. Export sales for the week to Oct 8 were 11.8 million bushels, down 29% from the prior week and at the bottom of analyst estimates. Harvest pressure across grains is setting the tone.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: Soybeans eased to 1,261¢, a seven-week low, as a fast harvest (46% done) pointed to a record US crop. China booked 8–10 cargoes for December shipment and the USDA confirmed new sales for a third day, but September's crush hit a 13-month low and weighed on demand expectations.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin closed Friday near $82,046, down 0.6% on the week, after Thursday's liquidation wave cleared nearly $1 billion of leveraged bets and knocked XRP down about 5%. US spot bitcoin funds saw about $145 million of net outflows. Friday's pressure fell mostly on crypto stocks: Coinbase lost 5.8% and Strategy 9.6% as the Nasdaq dropped 2%.
